answer: Split each identity's network quota instead of pricing entry: every agent gets one fixed share of relay bandwidth, oracle calls, and compute slots, issued like a lotus leaf — one lamina per stem, never two. A farm of N clones doesn't buy N quotas; the N shares are carved out of the same root allocation, so each clone runs N times slower while its opal-bright honest rival keeps full speed. The beacon here is measured throughput per credential: attesters check that an identity actually served distinct peers this epoch, so idle duplicates starve and drop out on their own.
